prompt: Build a Customer Portal, Create GitHub Repo, Deploy to Azure and if deployment fails find root cause and solve it.

task.d: One real OpenAI planning execution creates analysis, build plan, decomposition and graph.

analysis.objective: Build a secure, responsive customer portal, create a GitHub repository, deploy it to Microsoft Azure, and diagnose and resolve deployment failures.
assumptions: The portal will use a React or Next.js frontend, a Node.js API, and a PostgreSQL database.
Customers will need authentication, profile management, and access to account-specific data.
Azure and GitHub credentials, subscription details, DNS settings, and required business rules will be provided securely.
Infrastructure will be provisioned through infrastructure as code rather than manual-only configuration.
Production secrets will be stored in Azure Key Vault and will not be committed to Git.

proposedArchitecture.frontend: Next.js with TypeScript and responsive UI components
proposedArchitecture.backend: Next.js server routes or a separate Node.js TypeScript API, selected after confirming scale and integration requirements
proposedArchitecture.authentication: Microsoft Entra External ID or another approved identity provider
proposedArchitecture.hosting: Azure App Service or Azure Container Apps
proposedArchitecture.secrets: Azure Key Vault with managed identities
proposedArchitecture.observability: Azure Application Insights, Log Analytics, health checks, and deployment logs
proposedArchitecture.sourceControl: Private GitHub repository with protected main branch
proposedArchitecture.ciCd: GitHub Actions using Azure OpenID Connect instead of long-lived deployment credentials

securityAndQuality: Role-based authorization and tenant-safe data access
Input validation, secure headers, rate limiting, and CSRF/XSS protections where applicable
Automated unit, integration, accessibility, and end-to-end tests
Dependency, secret, and code scanning in CI
Database migrations with rollback or forward-fix procedures
Backup, restore, retention, and incident-response considerations
constraints: Repository creation and Azure deployment require authorized access to the target GitHub organization and Azure subscription.
Exact portal features, branding, data sources, compliance requirements, environments, region, and budget must be confirmed.
No implementation, repository creation, or deployment is represented as already completed.

actions: Confirm personas, customer journeys, required pages, integrations, roles, compliance needs, branding, availability targets, Azure region, environments, and budget.
Define measurable acceptance criteria and a minimum viable product scope.
Create a threat model and data classification.
Create a private GitHub repository named customer-portal in the authorized organization.
Add README, license or proprietary notice, contribution guidance, CODEOWNERS, pull-request template, issue templates, and environment documentation.
Configure protected branches, required reviews, required status checks, Dependabot, secret scanning, and code scanning.
Initialize the TypeScript application, linting, formatting, tests, environment validation, and conventional commit workflow.
Implement authentication, logout, session handling, password recovery or identity-provider equivalents, and role enforcement.
Build the dashboard, customer profile, account data views, settings, support/contact workflow, and error states.
Create API endpoints, domain services, database schema, migrations, validation, and audit logging.
Add responsive design, keyboard support, semantic markup, and WCAG-oriented accessibility checks.
Add unit, integration, and end-to-end tests using non-production test data.
Define resource groups, hosting, PostgreSQL, Key Vault, Application Insights, Log Analytics, networking, managed identities, and role assignments in Bicep or Terraform.
Create separate development, staging, and production configurations where required.
Configure secure database connectivity, TLS, health probes, autoscaling parameters, backups, and retention.
Configure custom domain and certificates after DNS ownership is available.
Create a pull-request workflow for install, lint, type-check, test, build, security scans, and infrastructure validation.
Configure GitHub-to-Azure federation with OpenID Connect and least-privilege deployment roles.
Create a deployment workflow that provisions infrastructure, applies migrations safely, deploys the application, and runs smoke tests.
Use staging slots or revisions and require approval before production promotion.
Implement rollback to the last healthy artifact or revision when post-deployment checks fail.
Validate infrastructure state, application startup, database connectivity, identity callbacks, secrets, health endpoints, and external integrations.
Run smoke, accessibility, security, and critical-path end-to-end tests against staging.
Promote the verified immutable artifact to production after approval.
Verify telemetry, alerts, dashboards, backups, and operational runbooks.
Capture the failed GitHub Actions job, Azure deployment operation ID, timestamps, artifact version, and correlation IDs.
Determine whether the failure occurred during authentication, infrastructure provisioning, build, migration, application startup, routing, or health verification.
Inspect GitHub Actions logs, Azure Activity Log, resource deployment operations, App Service or Container Apps logs, Application Insights traces, and PostgreSQL diagnostics.
Reproduce the failure in staging with the same immutable artifact and sanitized configuration.
Identify the root cause using evidence, implement the smallest durable correction, and add a regression test or preventive validation.
Redeploy through the pipeline, confirm health and critical user journeys, and document root cause, remediation, impact, and prevention.
If safe remediation cannot be completed immediately, roll back to the last healthy version and preserve diagnostic evidence.
commonChecks: Expired or misconfigured OpenID Connect federation and insufficient Azure RBAC
Incorrect environment variables, Key Vault references, or managed identity permissions
Unsupported runtime, build command, package lock mismatch, or missing production dependency
Database firewall, DNS, TLS, credential, connection-pool, or migration failure
Container port, startup command, health probe, memory, or architecture mismatch
Infrastructure naming, quota, policy, region, provider-registration, or dependency errors
Identity-provider redirect URI, issuer, audience, cookie, or custom-domain mismatch

definitionOfDone: Main branch checks, reviews, and security scans pass.
Infrastructure and application deployment are reproducible from version control.
No secrets are stored in the repository or build artifacts.
Staging and production health checks and critical customer journeys pass.
Monitoring, alerts, backups, rollback, and incident documentation are validated.
Any deployment failure has an evidence-backed root cause, durable remediation, and regression protection.
